summary: Paul David Numrich works in religious and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate at the University of Michigan in 1992. In 2006, he was attested at Loyola University Chicago and as Associate Professor at the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Debes (1906–2004) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He founded the Buddhistisches Seminar (1948), the Buddhistische Gesellschaft Hamburg (1954, serving on its board), and the Deutsche Buddhistische Union (1955), teaching Sister Vajirā and Hellmuth Hecker.

Paul Demiéville (1894–1979) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Lévi, Pelliot, and Chavannes. He taught at Xiamen University (1924–1926), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1945–1957), and held the Chinese chair at Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen (1845–1919) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, learning under Christian Lassen. He taught as a Privatdozent in Geneva and Berlin before becoming a professor at Kiel University in 1889.

Paul Dundas (1952–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He led Asian Studies at Edinburgh (around 1976–2017) and headed the Pali Text Society (around 1985–2023).
Paul Ekman (1934–2025) studied at New York University and Adelphi University. He held an academic post at the University of California, San Francisco from around 1960 to 2004.

Paul F. Knitter (born 1939) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and the University of Marburg, and later held a post at Union Theological Seminary from around 2007 to 2017.

Paul Fredericq (1850–1920) was a historian who studied at Ghent University and the University of Liège. He served as a professor at Liège (around 1879–1883) and Ghent University (from 1883), where he became rector in 1919.
Paul Fuller is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Bristol, studying under Rupert Gethin and Paul Dundas.

Paul G. Hackett works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied at Columbia University. His appointments include positions at the University of Virginia (attested 1994, 2003) and Columbia University (attested 2003, 2016).

Paul Groner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned his PhD from Yale University and studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor of religious studies at the University of Virginia (attested 1982–2010).

Paul Hacker (1913–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher educated in Bonn, Frankfurt, Heidelberg, and Berlin. He held the chair for Indology at the University of Bonn (1955–1963) and later the Indology chair at the University of Münster (1963–1978).

Paul Harrison is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Auckland and ANU under de Jong, Rajapatirana, and Hercus. He held positions at ANU, Auckland, Canterbury, and Stanford, where he became George Edwin Burnell Professor around 2007.
Paul Hoswell Hardacre (1915–2010) was a historian of Stuart England who studied at Stanford University and UCLA. He served as a faculty member at Vanderbilt University from around 1947 to 1980.

Paul J. Griffiths is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion who studied at Oxford and Wisconsin. He held posts at Notre Dame, the University of Chicago, the University of Illinois Chicago, and Duke University (around 2008–2017).
Paul Kingsbury is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).
Paul Kiparsky (born 1941) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at MIT under Morris Halle. He joined Stanford University around 1984.

Paul Loren Swanson (born 1951) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota, later serving as professor at Nanzan University (around 1986–2021).

Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University, working in religious studies, philosophy, and history. He served as director at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1999–2006) and professor of modern Jewish history and thought at the University of Chicago.

Paul Mus (1902–1969) studied in Paris under Lévi, Pelliot, and Mauss, working in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history. He held positions at the EFEO, École Pratique des Hautes Études, Collège de France (1946), and Yale University (1951).
